newsitem.title: ITALY: IMF wants Italy to pass extra budget-press reports.
newsitem.headline: IMF wants Italy to pass extra budget-press reports.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) believes Italy needs to raise 15 to 20 trillion lire through additional budgetary savings if it wants to keep alive its ambitions of joining a currency union by 1999, an Italian newspaper reported on Monday.

A team of IMF economists currently in Italy was working on the text of a letter to the Italian government which was expected to call for a supplementary budget to be passed and for a start to be made on pensions reform next year.

"The draft of the letter which (IMF) inspectors are working on refers clearly to an extra budget and also says it will not be possible to wait for 1998 to start dealing with pensions," Rome daily La Repubblica reported.
Under an agreement signed in 1995 between the former government led by Lamberto Dini and trade unions the current pensions system is not due to be reviewed until 1998.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi has called on the trade unions to join the goverment in initiating a fresh reform of pension arrangements next year.

The IMF team was expected to warn the government further revenue-raising measures and spending cuts would be needed if the ratio of the public sector deficit to gross domestic product (GDP) is to be cut to three percent by the end of 1997, Repubblica said.
The deficit-to-GDP target is one of the key criteria laid out in the 1991 Maastricht Treaty which plots a course towards monetary union.

"In the letter the IMF experts will probably indicate an exact figure for the supplementary budget (rumours talk of 15 to 20 trillion lire) and an unequivocal prescription -- cut pensions," Repubblica reported.

The government's 1997 budget, now making its way through parliament, calls for 62.5 trillion lire in deficit-cutting measures. Critics of the package say it places too much emphasis on tax-raising and not enough on slashing expenditure.

Italian newspapers also reported on Monday that EU Commissioner Mario Monti had said that a supplementary budget would be strictly necessary if Italy overshoots the official 1996 revised budget deficit target of 123.3 trillion lire.

"If the overshoot does not occur, the (extra) budget would seem to be unnecessary, but if there should be an overshoot it would seem to be not just possible but strictly necessary," Monti was quoted as saying by Corriere della Sera.
Independent economists forecast that the 1996 budget deficit will be at least 137 trillion lire, and some predict it could be as high as 140 trillion lire.
The government has so far declined to say whether it believes a supplementary budget is needed in early 1997.
